gallery.description: A contractor supporting U.S. Soldiers with the unit training equipment site, McCrady Training Center, S.C. Army National Guard in Eastover, S.C. assist in rail load of 29 M1A1 Abrams tanks in Columbia, S.C., June 19, 2014. The tanks will be transported by rail to a depot in California for final disposition. The S.C. Army National Guard was fielded the new M1A1 situational awareness Abrams tank in March 2014.  The older model M1A1 had been in the inventory since the early 1990s. (U.S. Air National Guard photo by Tech. Sgt. Jorge Intriago/Released)

gallery.title: File:20220810-RD-LSC-0330-Timelapse-5 4K.jpg
gallery.description:
Timelapse of free standing photovoltaic solar panel array at City Roots LLC, a family-owned local organic vegetable farm in Columbia, S.C, on August 10, 2022. The farm uses environmentally-friendly farming practices, including composting and offsetting its carbon footprint with three photovoltaic solar panel arrays. The U.S. Department of Agriculture USDA Rural Development RD helped them toward their energy goals with a Rural Energy for America Program REAP Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Loans and Grants Program grant of $20,000.00 toward a $99,060.00 31.2 kW solar array that produces 44,858 kWh (82%) per year and provides a $5,382 of savings per year. REAP loans, and grants assist farmers, ranchers, and rural small businesses in developing renewable energy systems and making energy-efficiency improvements to their operations. USDA Media by Lance Cheung.
For more information about the REAP program, please go to rd.usda.gov/programs-services/energy-programs/rural-energy-america-program-renewable-energy-systems-energy-efficiency-improvement-guaranteed-loans
